The mirror cannot be edited independently: tests/test_scaffold_data_in_sync.py byte-matches the two trees and fails (observed above), so satisfying AC3 means editing the canonical rule file this WU is forbidden to touch. Two clean resolutions, both a human call: (a) let T05 delete that sentence when it rewrites close-discipline.md, and re-scope AC3 here to `specfuse/loop/*.py tests/`; or (b) explicitly authorize T01 to remove the one clause naming the retired helper from both copies. Everything else in the WU is delivered, verified, and green in the working tree.

For each path: if it did NOT need changing, OMIT it from `files_changed` (declare only files you actually edit); if it SHOULD have changed, make the edit this attempt. A `(missing)` path was never created; a `(no diff)` path exists but is unchanged.

payload.agent_blocked_reason: Escalation trigger fires as written: 'Emit status: blocked if any consumer other than the four functions named above reads the debt marker; name it rather than leaving a dangling reader.' lint_plan.py:check_autoclose_debt_prediction is that consumer — it WARNs when a terminal close's body doesn't mention a predecessor gate's auto-close debt marker. Once the marker/heading machinery is deleted per this WU's spec, the check becomes permanently inert (its trigger condition can never occur again) and its own regex/prose keep AC2's grep nonzero. Deleting or rewriting it is outside the WU's authorized touch set (not named as a fifth function, and lint_plan.py isn't in Do-not-touch either — it's simply unaddressed). Needs an operator decision: fold it into the four-function scope (delete check_autoclose_debt_prediction + its two test files' coverage of it) or keep the marker string alive solely for this lint (which would make AC2 unsatisfiable as literally written).
